item: the scheduler's exclusive hold is counted, so a window that ends inside a standalone restore no longer releases the restore's hold (R383, OPEN_QUEUE 2026-10-27 item 23)
summary: BEFORE: BackgroundScheduler._exclusive_hold was one boolean. A standalone restore (src/backup/volume_job.py) claims it through the bare pause_for_exclusive_operation, which exclusive_window_open() cannot see; a diagnostics bundle opened inside it claimed the hold again and its resume released it, so Run now and Start were accepted mid-restore, and a Start the operator pressed during the restore was taken by the bundle's resume and started the loop mid-restore. NOW: hold_exclusive adds one claim and release_exclusive takes one off (floored at zero); _exclusive_hold reads count > 0; the fresh-claim reset of the deferred start happens only on 0 to 1; status() adds exclusive_holds so a claim never released is visible. resume_after_exclusive_operation, after its own release, asks the new defer_start(): when another operation still holds the machine it queues the start behind that hold and returns, so the outer operation's resume honours it. tests/test_scheduler_counted_hold.py drives a real BackgroundScheduler through the nested trace (4 of its 5 tests fail on the boolean). Stated limits: memstop and the data-drive move pause with no resume by design (the process ends), so their claim stays for the life of the process, as the boolean did; a future bare caller must release in a finally (R171) or its claim is permanent, which exclusive_holds in status() makes visible. Release-notes line: «A diagnostics bundle taken during a restore no longer lets collection restart in the middle of that restore.»
